newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends slightly higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Monday 0.03 percent higher with main trade on the official market in Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur.
The bourse all-share index closed at 636.58 points, up from 636.41 points on Friday.

"Except for BMCE, all other stocks had low volumes traded as people are keeping their money for their summer holidays rather than investing it on the stock exchange," a broker at BMCI Securities told Reuters.
BMCE rose three dirhams to 600 dirhams with 6,983 shares traded, brokers said.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams while Wafabank edged down two dirhams to 778 dirhams.
Morocco's biggest private conglomerate, ONA closed unchanged at 775 dirhams with 1,732 shares traded.
SNI, the second largest private group, rose five dirhams to 725 dirhams.
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued respectively in January and May 1996, dropped three and five dirhams to 1,352 and 1,170 dirhams.
"Privatisation bonds are losing ground as no flotation is planned soon," the BMCI broker added.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir dipped 5.50 dirhams to 345.50 dirhams with 3,759 shares exchanged.
Steel mill Sonasid fell 16 dirhams to 524 dirhams on profit-taking, the broker said.
Credit firm Credor fell 18 dirhams to 725 dirhams with just 78 shares changing hands.
Total traded volume on the official market was 22.3 million million dirhams, up from 21.8 dirhams, stockbrokers said.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 2.6 millon, down from 11 million dirhams. Main trade was in Imiter silver mine (SMI) with 2,698 shares exchanged.
